It is your responsibility to ensure that your detectors or other primary devices are properly installed, maintained, and tested regularly.

security.cameraSettings.soundDetection.u:
Test your smoke or carbon monoxide (CO) detectors to ensure they’re in working order and that your Secure camera can hear the alarms clearly.

 <emph>Tips:
</emph>
<ulist><litem>For smoke detectors: It must emit a T3 alarm pattern (three intermittent beeps followed by a pause). If you’re not sure, check the user manual of your smoke detector.</litem><litem>For CO detectors: It must emit a T4 alarm pattern (four intermittent beeps followed by a pause). If you’re not sure, check the user manual of your CO detector.</litem><litem>Make sure your camera is close enough to your safety detector to hear its alarm, which is usually a maximum of 6 m/19.5 ft. Make sure the camera is in the same room, not separated by doors or walls.</litem><litem>Enable your camera’s microphone in Camera settings.</litem><litem>Place your camera in an area where it will only hear one smoke detector and or carbon monoxide alarm at a time.</litem><litem>Avoid using this feature in a space that may echo, such as a room without furniture or a large room with high ceilings.</litem><litem>To test this feature, enable it in your Hue app, arm your system, and then press the Test button on your safety detector. The app needs to hear the test alarm for at least 20 seconds, so you may need to press the button more than once. </litem></ulist>

security.settings.cameraSettings.aiFeatu:
<emph>About the AI features</emph>
Your Hue Secure camera uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology to help you stay aware of what’s happening around your home. The AI features can detect and analyze activities and alert you in the Philips Hue App.

<emph>Activity: How it works</emph>
Hue Secure camera devices use Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology to automatically analyze the end-to-end encrypted footage and identify visual patterns that may look like people, packages, vehicles or animals. When the system detects one of these patterns, it can send you a notification alert in the app. These smart detection features are designed to help you stay informed, but may not always be accurate and should not replace your own awareness or safety measures.

<emph>Important to know</emph>
<ulist><litem>AI is helpful but not perfect. It may occasionally send false alerts or miss events due to factors like lighting, angles, or similar-looking objects or wrong camera positioning.</litem>

<litem>Notifications are meant to assist your awareness, not replace your own judgment. Always verify events yourself before acting on them (e.g., unlocking doors, calling emergency services, or granting access).</litem>

<litem>Performance can vary depending on environment, camera placement, internet connectivity, and other technical conditions.</litem>

<litem>This feature should not be relied upon as your only method of monitoring safety or security.</litem></ulist>

<emph>Your responsibility</emph>
Notifications are a supplementary tool. You remain responsible for monitoring your property and taking appropriate action based on the camera footage. Signify is not liable for damages, losses, or missed events that may result from reliance on AI features.

Sound detection requires a Secure plan. With the plan, the Hue app will alert you when your smoke alarm or carbon monoxide detector goes off. 

If your camera hears a smoke and or carbon monoxide alarm, it will automatically record the incident, send a notification to your mobile device, and turn on any lights that aren’t already on. Color-capable lights will change to red, while non-color-capable lights will change to warm white.

The camera starts recording when it recognizes the smoke alarm’s specific sound pattern. It will not send an alert unless it hears that pattern. Sound processing takes place locally in the camera itself.

security.setup.doorbell.mounting.install:
Choose the angle and determine the ideal height for the mount to securely attach the doorbell to the wall. Mark the spots, then drill holes into the wall.

Next, guide the wires from the wall through the center of the mount.

If you're having difficulty getting the mount flushed to the wall, add a spacer to make it easier to install.

Then screw the mount so it's flushed with the wall, but don't over tighten it.
